hypotheses.explanation: The extra world @ Diagonal((.76,.76,.76,1)) uniformly reduces mesh dimensions without reducing distances between primitive centers. The reported tabletop width is 2.5916 = 3.41 × 0.76. Structural meshes exhibit the same scaling, explaining the image discrepancy through a shared compiler mechanism.

camera_calibration.reason: set_view directly assigns the requested sensor width, 40.8; only numerical rounding is expected.

geometry_replay.reason: The apparent intended floor/wall width is 8.36/0.76 = 11. With root x scale 1.17, the maximum basis discrepancy should be approximately 11 × 1.17 × 0.24 = 3.0888, subject to replay frame details.

position_replay.reason: Right multiplication by this diagonal preserves translation; the supplied parent assignment restores matrix_world. No y-offset defect is evident.

visibility_isolation.reason: StudyPanel has an emitted mesh, and the visibility function recursively sets hide_render for both toggles.

support_relation.reason: With Floor.001 as the support surface and updated transforms, support_on corrects the measured AABB gap. Existing support bottoms already match floor top near -0.0264.

dependency_move.reason: All six bench meshes have their named part markers parented under StudyBench, consistent with the emitted hierarchy contract.

material_dependency.reason: Expected count is zero: mesh and material copies isolate edits, and the supplied Top.001 edit test passed. The interval allows an unreported ownership/runtime issue.

hypotheses.explanation: A camera framing mismatch with the desired image could contribute to the smaller overall apparent scene size. This is substantially weaker: current lens and sensor match the public specification, set_view assigns them directly, and camera framing alone cannot explain gaps between bench parts. The visible geometry scaling remains present even under this competing attribution.

camera_calibration.reason: A mismatch in desired framing or camera pose can coexist with correct sensor assignment. This scalar does not test pose or whether the public camera matches the desired image.

geometry_replay.reason: The explicit 0.76 basis multiplier still predicts approximately 3.0888 discrepancy regardless of whether camera framing also contributes.

position_replay.reason: Camera framing does not change emitted world translations; the supplied translation path appears correct.

visibility_isolation.reason: Camera framing does not change the recursive hide_render contract or StudyPanel mesh emission.

support_relation.reason: The AABB correction is independent of camera framing, assuming Floor.001 and evaluated transforms.

dependency_move.reason: The observed bench hierarchy remains intact independently of the camera.

material_dependency.reason: Expected count remains zero from ownership copying and the supplied passing edit test; camera attribution provides no reason to predict different edit behavior.

raw_evidence.source_scope: Actual SceneAct Blender compiler plus visibility/support/edit interfaces; controlled scene-description-to-Blender program repair, not natural-image end-to-end H

non_target.comparison: Exact direct comparison of matrices, local vertices, material values/nodes and parent; no hashes

raw_evidence.requirements: Compile a reusable SceneAct scene plan, retain intended world transforms and visibility, support composite furniture, preserve dependencies under group movement and local edits. Use images as desired appearance; investigate any shared module.

plan.reason: Choose disjoint pre-observation scalar prediction intervals; no predicted separation => no probe.
